title: post-build-inspector
intention: A post-build gate of python FILTERS judging orient's measurements — new failure, new filter — plus the one-time inference-free whole-repo sweep that brings the existing tree up to the gate so the sweep is never needed twice.
why: Akien's ruling 2026-07-27 ('the next thing is a post build inspector... we find a new thing, we add a new filter... we should only ever have to do that once'), and his older resignation that CC never adds logging until told — 'a post build inspector is just the thing' is the lever. Law 4: a filter at the gate is physics where CC's habit is policy.
traces_to: Law 4 — the lever itself: build-time refusal, not remembered discipline
Law 8 — proofs_exist; and the sweep findings refused a blanket-emit hollow fix
Law 7 — silent_device (MAP.md:434 enforced) and state_is_projection (the compiled-view drift check, the awaiting-physics IOU's other half)
Law 1 — a caught failure becomes a filter; the class stops recurring

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py (12 teeth) under the tester's MEASURED netns seal — validations/test_inspector.json, green, sealed. Durability: committed + pushed.
falsifier.proves_red: mirrors the charter; wrong-shape signal: a second genuinely-needed whole-repo sweep means the gate is not gating.
falsifier.horizon: edge (a) landed 2026-07-27 — 'CC runs it' became 'it refuses'. Next re-examine: when a candidate filter (edge c) is seeded by a real caught failure, or if a second whole-repo sweep is ever wanted (which would itself be the loudest finding).
